section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the request "Remember, Hashem, what has befallen us" as the plea of Knesses Yisrael, and contrasts it with Hashem's request to Israel to remember Him during the time of the Beis HaMikdash, the neglect of which caused the exile.
section.t: And to understand this, we must first preface an explanation of the request of Knesses Yisrael, "Remember, Hashem, what has befallen us; look and see our disgrace."
And the Baal Shem Tov explained,
"Remember, G-d, what has become of our Mah [the level of Mah] that is in the soul,
look and see and make us see our own shame."
This is the request of Knesses Yisrael from the Holy One, blessed be He.
And likewise, there is a request of remembrance from the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel,
as it is brought in the Zohar at the beginning of Parsha Bechukosai, on the verse, that this request from above
from Knesses Yisrael is also in the language of "Remember,"
as it is written,
"My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab plotted, and what Bilaam son of Beor answered him," etc.
And it concludes,
"What does Hashem ask of you? Only to do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly with your G-d."
And it is written,
"Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the sun grows dark," etc.
And it is brought in the Midrash,
"The prophet said to Israel: Remember your Creator as long as the Beis HaMikdash stands, which is called the House of Choice,
as long as the covenant of the Kehunah [Priesthood] stands,
as it is stated,
'And I chose him from all the tribes of Israel to be a priest to Me,'
as long as the covenant of the Levi'ah [Levites] stands,
as it is stated,
'For Hashem your G-d chose him from all your tribes.'"
And this is "before the sun grows dark,"
for "the sun grows dark" refers to the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash,
and it must be said, "Remember your Creator in the days of your youth,"
in the time of the Temple, which is called the House of Choice.
And since during the time of the Temple, Bnei Yisrael did not fulfill the request from above, "Remember your Creator," etc.,
"Remember now... to do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly with your G-d,"
this was the cause of the destruction,
and because of this, we request in the time of exile, "Remember, Hashem, what has befallen us; look and see our disgrace."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions the concept of remembrance in the context of the infinite, boundless nature of the Divine, explaining that while forgetfulness stems from limitation, remembrance is boundless, yet this makes the request for Divine remembrance seemingly incomprehensible.
section.t: And we need to understand what is the concept of remembrance Above, regarding which we request, "Remember, Hashem, what has befallen us."
For, behold,
remembrance and forgetfulness are concepts of boundlessness and boundary,
for the concept of forgetfulness is from the aspect of limitation,
since a human being is limited,
and from this aspect, all his matters are within limitation,
therefore, even the impression made upon him by a thing he saw or heard is within limitation, and because of this it is later interrupted,
which is the concept of forgetfulness.
However, the concept of remembrance is boundless,
as we see even in a human being,
that a matter which touches him in his innermost core and the pnimiyus of his soul,
that is,
that it is above his limitations,
he remembers it always.
According to this, it is not understood what is the content of the request, "Remember, Hashem," etc.,
for Above, He is boundless,
so why is it necessary to request the concept of remembrance from Above?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that remembrance and forgetfulness correspond to the aspects of "face" (panim) and "back" (achor) in the spiritual worlds, with Atzilus being the level of "face" where forgetfulness does not apply, while the souls of Israel are intrinsically at the level of "face" but due to the concealment of exile, they must request remembrance.
section.t: However, the concept is,
for, behold,
remembrance and forgetfulness are the concept of face and back,
pnimiyus and chitzoniyus,
and as it is in a human being below,
that a matter which touches him in his pnimiyus he remembers always,
but a matter that touches him only in his chitzoniyus
(which is the concept of back)
the concept of forgetfulness applies there.
And likewise, there are also Above, aspects of face, right, left, and back,
as it is brought in the Ramaz,
that they correspond to the four worlds of Atzilus, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah.
For, behold,
the world of Atzilus is called "face,"
for just as in the face of a human being there is the pnimiyus of vitality,
so too, in Atzilus is the pnimiyus of Ein Sof,
to the extent that He, His life, and His organs are one.
And this means,
that even though Atzilus is after the tzimtzum,
and the totality of the light after the tzimtzum is in the aspect of a contracted and limited line,
nevertheless,
it is the same essence of the light.
And this is the difference between Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah and Atzilus,
that the coming into being of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah is through the parsa,
but the coming into being of Atzilus is not through the parsa, but only through the tzimtzum,
as stated in Etz Chaim.
And the difference between tzimtzum and parsa is like the analogy of the difference we see below between light shining through a window or through a hole,
for even though the light is in diminution and contraction,
shining only to the measure that the window or hole can contain,
nevertheless, it is the same essence of the light,
but when light shines through a screen,
then the light is in a change of essence,
to the extent that the light that comes after the screen is called light of derivation.
And likewise, it is Above,
that the coming into being of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah through the parsa is in a change of essence,
but the coming into being of Atzilus through tzimtzum,
behold, even though the light there is in contraction,
nevertheless, it is the same essence of light as before the tzimtzum.
And even though in Atzilus there are also parsas,
as is known, there is a parsa between Kesser and Chochmah,
between Binah and Zeir Anpin, and between Zeir Anpin and Malchus,
nevertheless,
the parsa in Atzilus is not comparable to the parsas of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
for the parsas of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, their function is to conceal, and they conceal the light,
but the parsas in Atzilus reveal the light.
For, behold,
a parsa is like skin,
and Chazal said,
"These whose skin is like their flesh, the skin of a human being," etc.
(which is not like the skin of an animal, which is coarse skin),
and its analogue Above is the concept of the parsas that reveal the light.
And this is the difference between the letters of Mah
and the letters of Ban,
(and their concept in avodah is the difference between the letters of Torah and the letters of prayer),
for the letters of Ban conceal the light,
and from this aspect, the creations come into being as an entity and a separate thing,
but the letters of Mah do not conceal the light,
and on the contrary,
they reveal the light,
and therefore they effect bittul in the creations.
And this is "whose skin is like their flesh, the skin of a human being,"
for "Adam" [human being] in gematria is Mah,
and it is the concept of the parsas that reveal the light,
which are the parsas in Atzilus,
which are called by the name Mah,
as stated in the introduction to Tikkunei Zohar,
"The name Mah, which is the path of Atzilus."
And this is that Atzilus is called "face" because the revelation of Ein Sof shines there.
And the primary aspect of "face" is the aspect of Chochmah,
as in the verse,
"The wisdom of a man illuminates his face,"
and this means,
that in Atzilus, the light of Chochmah shines,
as per the statement,
"Abba Ilaah [the Supernal Father] dwells in Atzilus,"
and in Chochmah, Ein Sof shines,
as our master, the Alter Rebbe, stated in Tanya,
in the name of his teacher, the Maggid, that the level of Chochmah is that it alone is, and there is nothing besides Him,
and higher still,
that in Atzilus, the light of Kesser shines,
which is the concept of the name Mah, which is filled with alphin,
and Aleph is the Sefirah of Kesser.
And since Atzilus is the aspect of "face,"
the concept of forgetfulness does not apply there,
but in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, which are the aspect of "back,"
the concept of forgetfulness applies there.
And behold,
all this is the difference in the worlds,
but the souls of Israel, even when they are below, are in the aspect of pnimiyus,
for the souls of Israel arose in thought,
meaning in the most elevated level within thought,
and it is written,
"Face to face, Hashem spoke with you,"
for through this that Hashem spoke with you, the pnimiyus of Israel became the pnimiyus of Above.
However,
all this is from the aspect of the soul itself,
but from the aspect of its descent below and its enclothing in the body and the Nefesh HaBahamis, and especially in the time of exile,
in the time of exile it is written,
"And I will surely hide My face,"
and this means,
that since they turned their back to Me and not their face,
that is,
that the avodah was in the aspect of "back,"
therefore, even Above, there was a "hiding of the face,"
and from this aspect, it is necessary to request the concept of remembrance,
"Remember, Hashem, what has befallen us."
